<!-- ## Modelo  -->

<!-- AINDA NÃO FUNCIONA -->

<!-- $$ -->
<!-- Y_{i,t,d} \sim Pois(\lambda_{i,t,d}), \ \ i = 1,2; \ \ t = 1, \dots, T; \ \ d = 1, \dots, D \\ -->
<!-- log(\lambda_{i,t,d}) = \alpha_i + \beta_{t,i} + \gamma_{d,i} + \delta_t + \psi_d -->
<!-- $$ -->

<!-- A seguinte parametrização foi utilizada: -->

<!-- $$ -->
<!-- P(Y = y) = {y + \phi -1 \choose y} \left(\frac{\mu}{\mu + \phi}\right)^y\left(\frac{\phi}{\mu + \phi}\right)^{\phi} -->
<!-- $$ -->
<!-- Obs.: -->

<!--  - $Y_{1,t,d} \perp Y_{2,t,d} \ |\mathbf{\theta_{t,d}} \\$ -->

 
## Dados
```{r}
dados <- readRDS("Dados\\den_chik_2017_2019_RJ.RData")
dados <- dados %>% janitor::clean_names()

dados %>%

  summarise(y = n(), date = min(dt_sin_pri)) %>%
```

```{r}
data |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(epiweek = epiweek(dt_sin_pri), year = year(dt_sin_pri)) |>
  group_by(epiweek, year, delay, arbo) |>
  summarise(y = sum(y)) |> 
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = delay, values_from = y) |>
  mutate_if(~is.numeric(.), ~coalesce(.,0)) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = 4:19, names_to = "delay", values_to = "y") |>
  mutate(delay = as.numeric(delay)) |>
  arrange(year, epiweek, delay) |> 
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = arbo, values_from = y) -> data 

data %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  filter(year < 2019 | epiweek <= 20) %>% 
  mutate(chik_obs = ifelse(epiweek + delay > 20 & year == 2019, NA, Chik),
         den_obs = ifelse(epiweek + delay > 20 & year == 2019, NA, Den)) -> data_model
```



```{r}
data_model %>% 
  distinct(epiweek, year) %>% 
  mutate(time = 1:n()) %>% 
  inner_join(data_model, by = c("epiweek", "year")) -> data_model

y_new <- data_model %>% 
  mutate(report_time = time + delay) %>% 
  select(time, delay, report_time, y1_obs = chik_obs, y2_obs = den_obs, y1 = Chik, y2 = Den)
  

y_df <- y_new
```

## Modelo Bivariado 

```{r}
n <- nrow(y_df)

y_bvar <- matrix(NA, nrow = 2 * n, ncol = 2)
y_bvar[1:n, 1] <- y_new$y1_obs
y_bvar[n + 1:n, 2] <- y_new$y2_obs

I <- matrix(NA, nrow = 2 * n, ncol = 2)
I[1:n, 1] <- 1
I[n + 1:n, 2] <- 1


fixed_covariate = data.frame(alphai = as.factor(c(rep(1, n), rep(2, n))),
                             id_time1 = c(rep(1,n), rep(NA, n)),
                             id_delay1 = c(rep(1,n), rep(NA, n)),
                             id_time2 = c(rep(NA, n), rep(1, n)),
                             id_delay2 = c(rep(NA, n), rep(1, n)),
                             idrep = rep(1:2, each = n))


random_covariate <- list(time1  = c(y_df$time, rep(NA, n)),
                         delay1 = c(y_df$delay, rep(NA, n)),
                         time2  = c(rep(NA, n), y_df$time),
                         delay2 = c(rep(NA, n), y_df$delay),
                         time = rep(y_df$time, 2),
                         delay = rep(y_df$delay, 2))


Y = y_bvar
joint_data <- cbind(Y, fixed_covariate, random_covariate)


joint_model <- Y ~ -1 + alphai +
  + f(time,  model = "ar1", replicate = idrep,
      hyper = list(prec = list(param = c(0.001, 0.001)))) +
  + f(delay, model = "ar1", replicate = idrep) +
  + f(time1, model = "ar1") +
  + f(time2, copy  = "time1", fixed = TRUE) + 
  + f(delay1, model = "ar1") +
  + f(delay2, copy  = "delay1", fixed = TRUE) 


output0 <- INLA::inla(joint_model, family = rep("nbinomial", 2),
                      data = joint_data,
                      control.predictor = list(link = 1, compute = T),
                      control.compute = list( config = T, waic=F, dic=F),
                      control.family = list(
                        list(hyper = list("theta" = list(prior = "loggamma", param = c(0.001, 0.001)))),
                        list(hyper = list("theta" = list(prior = "loggamma", param = c(0.001, 0.0001))))
                      )
                      
)
```

## Amostragem da preditiva e nowcasting

```{r}

samples <- INLA::inla.posterior.sample(n = 1000, output0)



index_missing <- which(is.na(joint_data$`1`) & is.na(joint_data$`2`))


vector_samples_bvar <- lapply(X = samples,
                              FUN = function(x, idx = index_missing, n = 1984){
                                idx_1 <- idx[idx <= n]
                                idx_2 <- idx[idx > n]
                                unif.log = 1
                                
                                y1 <- stats::rnbinom(n = idx_1,
                                                     mu = exp(x$latent[idx_1]),
                                                     size = x$hyperpar[1]
                                ) * unif.log
                                
                                y2 <- stats::rnbinom(n = idx_2,
                                                     mu = exp(x$latent[idx_2]),
                                                     size = x$hyperpar[2]
                                ) * unif.log
                                
                                return(cbind(y1,y2))
                              } )


gg.age <- function(x, dados.gg, idx, n = 1984){
  idx_1 <- idx[idx <= n]
  idx_2 <- idx[idx > n]
  data.aux <- dados.gg
  Tmin <- min(dados.gg$time[idx])
  data.aux$`1`[idx_1] <- x[,1]
  data.aux$`2`[idx_2] <- x[,2]
  data.aggregated <- data.aux |>
    ## Selecionando apenas os dias faltantes a partir
    ## do domingo da respectiva ultima epiweek
    ## com dados faltantes
    dplyr::filter(time >= Tmin  ) |>
    dplyr::group_by(time) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      Y1 = sum(`1`, na.rm = T), 
      Y2 = sum(`2`, na.rm = T), .groups = "keep" 
    )
  data.aggregated
}

## Step 4: Applying the age aggregation on each posterior
tibble.samples.0 <- lapply(X = vector_samples_bvar,
                           FUN = gg.age,
                           dados = joint_data,
                           idx = index_missing)


srag.pred.0 <- dplyr::bind_rows(tibble.samples.0, .id = "sample")

total.summy <- srag.pred.0 |>
  dplyr::group_by(time, sample) |>
  dplyr::summarise(Y1 = sum(Y1, na.rm = T),
                   Y2 = sum(Y2, na.rm = T)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(Median_y1 = stats::median(Y1, na.rm = T),
                   LI_y1  = stats::quantile(Y1, probs = 0.025, na.rm = T),
                   LS_y1  = stats::quantile(Y1, probs = 0.975, na.rm = T),
                   LIb_y1 = stats::quantile(Y1, probs = 0.25, na.rm = T),
                   LSb_y1 = stats::quantile(Y1, probs = 0.75, na.rm = T),
                   Median_y2 = stats::median(Y2, na.rm = T),
                   LI_y2  = stats::quantile(Y2, probs = 0.025, na.rm = T),
                   LS_y2  = stats::quantile(Y2, probs = 0.975, na.rm = T),
                   LIb_y2 = stats::quantile(Y2, probs = 0.25, na.rm = T),
                   LSb_y2 = stats::quantile(Y2, probs = 0.75, na.rm = T),
                   .groups = "drop")



dados_by_week <- y_new |>
  group_by(time) |>
  summarise(y1 = sum(y1, na.rm = T),
            y2 = sum(y2, na.rm = T))

summary_bivar <- total.summy
```

## Análises univariadas

### Chikungunya 
```{r}
dados_chik <- y_new %>% 
  select(time, delay, report_time, Y = y1_obs, count = y1)


model <- Y ~ 1 +
  f(time,
    model = "ar1",
    hyper = list("prec" = list(prior = "loggamma",
                               param = c(0.001, 0.001))
    )) +
  f(delay, model = "ar1",
    hyper = list("prec" = list(prior = "loggamma",
                               param = c(0.001, 0.001)))
  )

output_chik <- INLA::inla(model, family = "nbinomial",
                          data = dados_chik,
                          control.predictor = list(link = 1, compute = T),
                          control.compute = list(config = T, waic=F, dic=F),
                          control.family = list(
                            hyper = list("theta" = list(prior = "loggamma",
                                                        param = c(0.001,
                                                                  0.001))
                                         )
                            )
                          )


ts.plot(output0$summary.random$time1$`0.5quant` + output0$summary.random$time$`0.5quant`[vectime], main = "Efeito do tempo") #, ylim = c(-6, 9))
lines(output_chik$summary.random$time$`0.5quant`, col = 2)#, ylim = c(-6, 9))
legend("topleft", lty = 1, col = 1:2, legend = c("Bivariado", "Univariado"))

ts.plot(output0$summary.random$delay1$`0.5quant` + output0$summary.random$delay$`0.5quant`[1:16], main = "Efeito do Delay", xlab = "Delay")
lines(output_chik$summary.random$delay$`0.5quant`, col = 2)
legend("topright", lty = 1, col = 1:2, legend = c("Bivariado", "Univariado"))

```


```{r}
index.missing <- which(is.na(dados_chik$Y))


## Step 1: Sampling from the approximate posterior distribution using INLA
srag.samples0.list <- INLA::inla.posterior.sample(n = 1000, output_chik)

## Give a parameter to trajectories, TO-DO

## Step 2: Sampling the missing triangle from the likelihood using INLA estimates
vector.samples0 <- lapply(X = srag.samples0.list,
                          FUN = function(x, idx = index.missing){
                            # if(zeroinflated){
                            #   unif.log <- as.numeric(runif(idx,0,1) < x$hyperpar[2])
                            # }else{
                            unif.log = 1
                            # }
                            stats::rnbinom(n = idx,
                                           mu = exp(x$latent[idx]),
                                           size = x$hyperpar[1]
                            ) * unif.log
                          } )

## Step 3: Calculate N_{a,t} for each triangle sample {N_{t,a} : t=Tactual-Dmax+1,...Tactual}

gg.age <- function(x, dados.gg, idx){
  data.aux <- dados.gg
  Tmin <- min(dados.gg$time[idx])
  data.aux$Y[idx] <- x
  data.aggregated <- data.aux |>
    ## Selecionando apenas os dias faltantes a partir
    ## do domingo da respectiva ultima epiweek
    ## com dados faltantes
    dplyr::filter(time >= Tmin  ) |>
    dplyr::group_by(time) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      Y = sum(Y), .groups = "keep"
    )
  data.aggregated
}

## Step 4: Applying the age aggregation on each posterior
tibble.samples.0 <- lapply( X = vector.samples0,
                            FUN = gg.age,
                            dados = dados_chik,
                            idx = index.missing)

srag.pred.0 <- dplyr::bind_rows(tibble.samples.0, .id = "sample")

#return(srag.pred.0)



total.summy <- srag.pred.0 |>
  dplyr::group_by(time, sample) |>
  dplyr::summarise(Y = sum(Y, na.rm = T)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(Median = stats::median(Y, na.rm = T),
                   LI = stats::quantile(Y, probs = 0.025, na.rm = T),
                   LS = stats::quantile(Y, probs = 0.975, na.rm = T),
                   LIb = stats::quantile(Y, probs = 0.25, na.rm = T),
                   LSb = stats::quantile(Y, probs = 0.75, na.rm = T),
                   .groups = "drop")


output<- list()
output$total <- total.summy

summary_chik <- total.summy

dados_by_week <- dados_chik |> 
  group_by(time) |> 
  summarise(n = sum(count, na.rm = T))

output$total |> 
  left_join(data_real, by = "time") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = date, y = Median, col = 'Nowcasting')) +
  geom_line(data = data_real %>% filter(time > 100), aes(date, y = y1, col = 'Observed')) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = LI, ymax = LS, col = NA), alpha = 0.2, show.legend = F) +
  geom_line() +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c('grey50', 'black'), name = '')+
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = '2 weeks', date_labels = '%V/%y', name = 'Date in Weeks')+
  labs(x = '', y = 'Nº Cases')
```

```{r}
    ## do domingo da respectiva ultima epiweek
    ## com dados faltantes
    dplyr::filter(time >= Tmin  ) |>
    dplyr::group_by(time) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      Y = sum(Y), .groups = "keep"
    )
  data.aggregated
}

## Step 4: Applying the age aggregation on each posterior
tibble.samples.0 <- lapply( X = vector.samples0,
                            FUN = gg.age,
                            dados = dados_deng,
                            idx = index.missing)

srag.pred.0 <- dplyr::bind_rows(tibble.samples.0, .id = "sample")


total.summy <- srag.pred.0 |>
  dplyr::group_by(time, sample) |>
  dplyr::summarise(Y = sum(Y, na.rm = T)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(Median = stats::median(Y, na.rm = T),
                   LI = stats::quantile(Y, probs = 0.025, na.rm = T),
                   LS = stats::quantile(Y, probs = 0.975, na.rm = T),
                   LIb = stats::quantile(Y, probs = 0.25, na.rm = T),
                   LSb = stats::quantile(Y, probs = 0.75, na.rm = T),
                   .groups = "drop")


output<- list()
output$total <- total.summy

summary_dengue <- total.summy

dados_by_week <- dados_deng |> 
  group_by(time) |> 
  summarise(n = sum(count, na.rm = T))


output$total |> 
  left_join(data_real, by = "time") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = date, y = Median, col = 'Nowcasting')) +
  geom_line(data = data_real %>% filter(time > 100), aes(date, y = y2, col = 'Observed')) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = LI, ymax = LS, col = NA), alpha = 0.2, show.legend = F) +
  geom_line() +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c('grey50', 'black'), name = '')+
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = '2 weeks', date_labels = '%V/%y', name = 'Date in Weeks')+
  labs(x = '', y = 'Nº Cases')
```


 - Dúvida: se a gente tá estimando até 15 semanas de atraso, é ok comparar com o dado real de mais de 15 semanas? Já que o intervalo é para o dado observado até a 15° semana de atraso, certo?
 
 - Podemos fazer comparações mais espertas entre os efeitos estimados? Talvez pensando na distribuição em vez de somente na mediana?
 
# Avaliando modelos

## Dengue

### Medidas de erro (usando a mediana como estimativa pontual)
```{r}
library(metrica)

obs_dengue <- data_real %>% 
  filter(time >= 110) %>% 
  pull(y2)

pred_dengue_uni <- summary_dengue$Median
pred_dengue_biv <- summary_bivar$Median_y2

cbind(metrics_summary(obs = obs_dengue, 
                      pred = pred_dengue_uni, metrics_list = c("MAPE", "MAE", "MSE"),
                      type= "regression"),
      metrics_summary(obs = obs_dengue, 
                      pred = pred_dengue_biv, metrics_list = c("MAPE", "MAE", "MSE"),
                      type= "regression")) %>% 
  knitr::kable(digits = 2) %>% 
  kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width = F) %>% 
  kableExtra::add_header_above(header = c("Univariado" = 2, "Bivariado" = 2))
      

plot_uni <- scatter_plot(obs = obs_dengue, 
                         pred = pred_dengue_uni, 
                         orientation = "PO",
                         print_metrics = T,
                         metrics_list = c("MAPE", "MAE", "MSE")
                         ) + ggtitle("Univariado") + theme_light()

plot_bi <- scatter_plot(obs = obs_dengue, 
                         pred = pred_dengue_biv, 
                         orientation = "PO",
                         print_metrics = T,
                         metrics_list = c("MAPE", "MAE", "MSE")
                         ) + ggtitle("Bivariado") + theme_light()

plot_uni + plot_bi
```

### Intervalos

 - Ideia a fazer: olhar melhor para as preditivas 
 
```{r}
summary_dengue %>% 
  mutate(Model = "Univariado") -> summary_dengue 

summary_bivar %>% 
  select(time, contains("_y2")) %>% 
  mutate(Model = "Bivariado") -> bivar_dengue

colnames(bivar_dengue) <- colnames(summary_dengue)

dengue_models_summary <- bind_rows(summary_dengue, bivar_dengue) 

dengue_models_summary %>% 
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = time, y = Median, ymin = LI, ymax = LS, col = Model) +
  #ggdist::stat_pointinterval()
  ggdist::geom_pointinterval(size = 2, position = position_dodge(width = .6)) 



dengue_models_summary %>% 
  mutate(int_size_95 = LS - LI,
         int_size_50 = LSb - LIb) %>% 
  group_by(Model) %>% 
  summarise(mean_int_size_95 = mean(int_size_95),
            mean_int_size_50 = mean(int_size_50))
  
dengue_models_summary %>% 
  mutate(int_size_95 = LS - LI,
         int_size_50 = LSb - LIb) %>% 
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = time, y = int_size_95, col = Model) +
  geom_line(size = .8) +
  labs(title = "Comprimento dos intervalos de 95% de credibilidade") +
  theme_light() -> gg_int_90

dengue_models_summary %>% 
  mutate(int_size_95 = LS - LI,
         int_size_50 = LSb - LIb) %>% 
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = time, y = int_size_50, col = Model) +
  geom_line(size = .8) +
  labs(title = "Comprimento dos intervalos de 50% de credibilidade") +
  theme_light() -> gg_int_50


gg_int_90 

gg_int_50


```


### Interval score

$score = (upper - lower) + \frac{2}{\alpha}(lower - true)*\mathbf{1}(true < lower) + \frac{2}{\alpha}(true - upper)*\mathbf{1}(true > upper)$

```{r}

dengue_models_summary |> 
  mutate(score_95 = interval_score(true_values = rep(obs_dengue, 2), 
                                   lower = LI, upper = LS, interval_range = 95),
         score_50 = interval_score(true_values = rep(obs_dengue, 2), 
                                   lower = LIb, upper = LSb, interval_range = 50)) -> dengue_models_summary


dengue_models_summary |> 
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = time, y = score_95, colour = Model) +
  geom_line(size = .8) +
  labs(y = "Score para o intervalo de 95% de credibilidade",
       colour = "Modelo") +
  theme_light()
```
